title: Bodybuilding is GAY? (BREAKING DOWN Andrew Tate)
summary: In part one NH rebuts the claim that bodybuilding is gay. Pro bodybuilding is a tiny niche, caring about your looks is not feminine, and men who mock it are usually projecting insecurity. Muscle can also buy peace by deterring fights. In part two he breaks down Andrew Tate's psychology and business model (webcam scam, Hustlers University, affiliate spam, opportunistic Islam) as an example of algorithm-promoted masculinity gurus who exploit alienated young men.
claims: Pro bodybuilding on stage is under 0.1% of bodybuilding; anyone who trains for looks is a bodybuilder without ever competing
Bodybuilding is not a beauty pageant: pageants judge faces, while ugly men like Ronnie Coleman win on their body
Calling looks-focused training feminine pushes men to be slobs, makes them less attractive and breeds resentment
Men who do calisthenics or martial arts and post shirtless photos also train for looks; getting aesthetics as a byproduct is no different
The ancient Greeks valued male beauty as well as strength; Socrates said it is a shame to grow old without seeing the beauty and strength one's body is capable of
The virtuous way for a man to become more beautiful is strengthening and building muscle, not surgery or consumerist routines; bodybuilding develops body and mind
Men who mock bodybuilding or call it gay are usually projecting insecurity about their looks or sexuality
His small boxing teacher (5'4", 130 lb) was always cordial because he was secure; the men who gave NH a hard time for his size were insecure
Bodybuilding is not a sport because it is judged on aesthetics, not performance, so comparing it to martial arts makes no sense
Ridicule is used when there is no logical argument; where there is resentment there is no logic
He did martial arts but chose bodybuilding because he lacked the bloodlust and aggressiveness needed to excel at fighting
Bullied as a kid, he became aggressive and started attacking others; bodybuilding and fixing his body ended that spiral and gave him peace
Looking muscular deters fights: predators pick victims, not lions; muscles buy peace, and street fights involve knives and bottles
The ideal is to both look intimidating and know how to fight
Masculinity gurus show money, girls and cigars to sell you an image; judge influencers by their motivations and actions, not their words
Tate says that at age 5-6 a chess opponent's crying made him happier than winning, which suggests sadism or a lack of empathy
Narcissists usually have low self-esteem and feed their egos through others' attention
Tate ran a webcam business that he described as scamming lonely men, then Hustlers University selling dropshipping and crypto courses with a pyramid-like affiliate program
Tate became famous because his paying members were told to flood social media with clips of him; we live in an 'algorithmocracy' where algorithms, not merit, decide who rises
Influencers profit from keeping young men alienated and resentful; solving their problems would lose them as customers
Hustle culture feeds on alienation and makes men work harder for the very system they resent
Misogyny among young men usually comes from fear of rejection and loneliness; the problem lies within, and blaming women only deepens it
Most masculinity gurus have no lasting relationships or families; men should seek to love and understand women
Masculinity influencers are probably mostly on steroids, which makes mocking vanity hypocritical
stats: about 210 lb (20 lb heavier than Tate's ~190)
